verses.text: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.
By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments.
For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.
For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.
Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood. It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
For there are three who testify :
the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one.
If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater; for this is God’s testimony which he has testified concerning his Son.
He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.
The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.
These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.
This is the boldness which we have toward him, that, if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us.
And if we know that he listens to us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him.

If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life for those who sin not leading to death. There is a sin leading to death. I don’t say that he should make a request concerning this.
All unrighteousness is sin, and there is a sin not leading to death.
We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him.
We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true, and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.

footnotes.content: The beginning of faith is so simple—just believing Jesus is the Christ. When a soul turns to Him, something changes deep down; we become God's children. And watch how quickly love flows: first to the Father, then immediately to His other children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Love isn't a feeling that comes and goes. Here John puts his finger on the test: Do you keep His commandments? That's where you know if you truly love God and His children. The proof lives in what you do, not what you say.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I've learned that His commandments aren't chains but guardrails. They seem hard only until you walk with Him long enough to see they're made for our freedom. Love that keeps His word finds that the yoke is easy and the burden light.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The world wants to tell us what to love, what to fear, what matters. But look—everyone born of God has already won. The victory isn't in the future; it's here now in faith itself. That's what overcomes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: John asks a simple question, but it cuts right to the heart: Who is the overcomer? Not the one with the loudest voice or the strongest will, but the one who has made Jesus his Lord. That belief is the victory itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Water and blood—His baptism and His crucifixion. Jesus didn't come with empty words, but in the reality of a human life, suffering, dying, rising. The Spirit bears witness to what our eyes couldn't see and our hearts struggle to believe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three witnesses—Spirit, water, blood—all testifying to the same truth. God has left us no excuse to doubt. He didn't ask us to guess or hope. He gave us testimony that speaks on every side.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The three agree as one. What harmony there is in God's witness! Not a single note of contradiction. When your heart finally quiets long enough to hear them all at once, doubt loses its grip.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We believe human testimony about the simple things—what we're told day by day. But to reject God's testimony about His own Son? That would be the deepest foolishness. His word carries a weight that trumps all else.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Belief isn't just head knowledge; it's receiving God's testimony into your whole self. When you believe in Jesus, you don't just know about Him—you carry His witness within you. Refusal to believe accuses God Himself of lying.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is the heart of it: God's testimony is a gift of eternal life itself. Not a reward we earn, but a life already given to us in His Son. To know Christ is to have already stepped into forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The division is clear and final: you either have the Son or you don't. There's no middle ground, no 'almost.' The whole of eternal life hinges on this one relationship. Everything you need is in Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: John writes so we won't drift in doubt. He's giving us certainty—knowledge that we have eternal life right now, not someday. And that knowledge is meant to anchor us in continued faith in His name. Assurance and obedience belong together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prayer isn't supposed to be timid. We have boldness—a word meaning open-hearted, unashamed access to God's presence. But listen: boldness isn't presumption. It's asking 'according to His will,' honoring His mind over our own wishes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do you hear the transformation? If we know He listens—and He does—then what we ask for is already ours in principle. Faith isn't about begging a reluctant God. It's about trusting that He's already inclined toward His children's good.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seeing a brother stumble breaks the heart. Here John calls us to intercession—to stand in the gap and ask God to restore what was broken. There's a depth of care in that asking. We hold each other up.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sin is sin, and it stains us all. But not all sin leads to death—to final separation from God. The distinction matters because it tells us that repentance and restoration are always possible until we refuse them altogether.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here's the mystery: born of God, we keep ourselves from habitual sin. Not by white-knuckling, but because something in us has changed. The evil one hasn't lost his power, but he can't touch those guarded by Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A hard truth: the world is held in the grip of darkness. But notice—we are of God. We're on a different story. To belong to Him is to stand apart from the world's default darkness, even while we live within it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: we have been given understanding. Not everyone sees, but those born into God's family receive eyes to recognize Him. In Christ, we enter the true reality—and we remain there, secure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A closing whisper, almost tender: keep yourselves from idols. After all this talk of eternal life and God's presence, John knows what steals the heart—false lovers, false securities, false gods. Stay faithful to the true One.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
